info.name: HabitLoop | Backend API
info.description: Import this collection directly; no separate environment is needed. Start the backend, then run Setup → Owner signup and Setup → Member signup. Run requests in the numbered folders in order to populate IDs. Requests save tokens and resource IDs as collection variables on successful responses. Negative, internal, SSE, and destructive cases are explicitly labeled. Never use the local internal key or demo credentials in production.

item.name: 00 · Health
item.description: Public health checks for every service.

item.name: 01 · Setup & authentication
item.description: Start here. Signups create fresh, unique demo identities and save their JWTs. Owner and member are in public; other tenant is acme.

item.name: 02 · Habits & completions
item.description: Create the daily habit before running dependent requests. A separate weekly and mismatch habit demonstrate schedule and category variations.

item.name: 03 · Communities, invitations & challenges
item.description: Create communities and challenge as owner. Member requests explicitly use the member token. Create a fresh invitation before accepting or declining it.

item.name: 09 Create second invite for decline demo

exec: pm.test('Owner has two manual completions', () => pm.expect(entry.count).to.eql(2));

item.name: Negative · other tenant cannot view community
Negative · private community cannot be joined directly
04 · Wearable integrations
item.description: Connect an owned habit. The device key is returned only at connection creation and saved in a collection variable. Event acceptance is 202; inspect event history for PROCESSED or REJECTED.

exec: pm.test('One processed event for duplicate deliveries', () => { pm.expect(sent).to.have.lengthOf(1); pm.expect(sent[0].status).to.eql('PROCESSED'); });
pm.test('Invalid samples were rejected', () => pm.expect(events.filter(x => x.status === 'REJECTED').length).to.be.at.least(3));

item.name: Negative · member cannot view owner's events
Negative · member cannot disconnect owner's connection
05 · Analytics & recommendations
item.description: Dashboard and trend use the caller's JWT. SSE remains open and should be sent separately, not run as part of a collection runner.

exec: pm.test('Manual and wearable logs reached analytics', () => { pm.expect(habit.todayCount).to.eql(5); pm.expect(habit.doneToday).to.eql(true); });

item.name: Negative · trend range out of bounds
06 · Internal service contracts
item.description: Trusted internal routes, intentionally separate from user-facing requests. They require X-Internal-Key; use only in the local demo or private network. Activity uses the same logId to demonstrate idempotence.

exec: pm.test('Duplicate analytics delivery did not increment count', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().count).to.eql(5));

07 · Live updates (manual only)
item.description: Long-lived SSE connections do not complete like normal requests. Run separately, not as part of a collection run.

request.description: Long-lived SSE connection. It closes on token expiry or server timeout; send separately.

item.name: 99 · Cleanup (destructive)
item.description: Run manually and last: these requests disconnect the wearable or delete habits. They invalidate dependencies used by other folders.
